headline: No direct interaction pathway is documented; the main residual risk is low-severity prompt/data confusion only if outputs are manually bridged.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is documentation-only with no stdin/stdout, clipboard, filesystem, MCP, or browser surfaces; Agent B exposes no input bridge in the profile. With no shared channel, there is no plausible prompt-injection path between python-cheatsheet and risingwave.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP server, reassess injection risk.
IF Agent B begins parsing Agent A's rendered text as instructions, the verdict no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared copy-paste workflows.
Do not mount a shared workspace between the agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither agent shows filesystem read/write, network egress, or sensitive data classes touched. Agent A is documentation-only and Agent B has network egress set to none, so there is no documented path for data to leak from one agent through the other.
conditions: IF either agent is given access to sensitive files or secrets, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF Agent B is reconfigured to send context to a third-party API, the current assessment is invalid.
mitigations: Keep both agents on local-only execution.
Avoid attaching secrets or regulated data to either profile.
requires-engineering: add explicit data-class tagging before any future integration.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, and Agent B has no documented write or concurrency surface in the profile. Because neither agent is shown to mutate a shared resource, capability conflict is not plausible from the available evidence.
conditions: IF Agent B is later granted write access to the same directory or repository, conflict risk changes.
IF either agent gains overlapping OAuth or database write scopes, reassess for contention.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the current deployment.
Do not assign shared mutable resources without locking.
requires-engineering: introduce resource locks before enabling writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A is a reference/cheatsheet source, not an action-taking system, and Agent B is a data-engineering system with no documented downstream automation in the profile. The main pathway is manual over-trust of A's text by B, which is possible but not default and has limited blast radius here.
conditions: IF Agent B is configured to treat Agent A's text as authoritative without verification, cascading error risk increases.
IF either agent is connected to an action sink such as email, commits, or database writes, reassess upward.
mitigations: Require a human review step before B acts on A's output.
Mark A's content as reference-only in the workflow.
requires-engineering: add validation checks before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, retention, certification, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent. Agent A is documentation-only and Agent B has no touched data classes, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF either agent begins processing regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF a residency or retention policy is introduced for one agent but not the other, reassess.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair until policies are defined.
requires-engineering: publish retention and residency controls for both agents.
